# Caddy — load-balancer

Two backends with sticky sessions via `lb_policy cookie ROUTEID`, an affinity cookie Caddy synthesizes itself (an HMAC of the upstream address), so the backends need no Tomcat jvmRoute. APP_NAME distinguishes which one served the page.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Caddy site block (`caddy/http/load-balancer/vaadin.caddyfile`), mounted as
`/etc/caddy/vaadin.caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
# Two backends behind one site, with sticky sessions.
#
# Vaadin needs affinity: the session lives in one backend's memory, so a request
# that lands on the other one finds no UI. Caddy synthesizes its own affinity
# cookie rather than reading a route id out of JSESSIONID, so — as in every
# other tree — the backends need no Tomcat jvmRoute. APP_NAME is what
# distinguishes them in the rendered page.
#
# The cookie's value is an HMAC of the chosen upstream's address rather than a
# readable server id (HAProxy's `v1`); its name is ROUTEID to match the other
# trees, and Caddy writes it as `Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`. A request
# without the cookie, or whose upstream has gone, falls back to a random pick.
#
# No health checks, deliberately: a backend that refused a connection while it
# was still booting is not blacklisted, so the startup race CLAUDE.md describes
# for NGINX and Apache does not arm here — that request is answered 502 and the
# next one is tried afresh.
:80 {
	import common
	reverse_proxy vaadin-1:8080 vaadin-2:8080 {
		lb_policy cookie ROUTEID
	}
}
```

The global options and the `common` snippet this file imports (the
access log and the compression allowlist) come from the shared
[Caddyfile](../../Caddyfile), mounted read-only over the image's own
`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`. It imports this file, so the two only load as a pair.
